name: Yusuf Gupta

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers stay confidential. What is an ordinary day on the appliance service line like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The first call is usually someone with a fridge that stopped cooling overnight. I write the model number in my paper book before opening the warranty screen, because a wrong digit can send a repairer to the wrong house. I have done this for years and I like fixing a real problem, but the queue timer makes every careful question feel slow.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And outside the line, what does the pay have to carry?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Mira, my partner, does alterations and her orders rise and fall with the season. Our daughter is grown and has her own rent, so I don't put her wages in our sums. We have about four months of expenses saved; that is useful, though at fifty-eight I watch what happens to the next working years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team I can live with a little less copying between screens. The hard part is hearing which part failed before I promise a visit. A quicker form is fine if it leaves me time to listen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I don't believe the queue will suddenly become easy. My calls should still be there, but Mira's sewing orders vary and four months saved isn't a long holiday. I don't want another monthly bill just because a vendor says the machine will save us time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I'll keep the same warranty rota and use my paper model-number check before submitting a repair request. I'll move a small fixed amount from each pay packet into the reserve while the shifts hold. If the plateau carries on into its first year, I'll keep doing those calls and the same transfer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, a little. The wage looks steady in this picture, but I already count the months in the savings account. I can manage a plain week; I just don't want a surprise bill on top.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you write in that book that the screen misses?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Serial digits and the customer's own words about the noise. A tick box doesn't tell the engineer whether the fridge clicks twice or hums all night. I can show a new agent the page without giving them my whole book.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your daughter to help if a bill arrived?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughter pays her own rent, so her grown-up life shouldn't be our spare account. Mira and I would use the reserve for a genuine repair bill before asking her for money.

say: I'd welcome **quicker forms** if they leave time to listen.
I'd keep **model numbers** and customer details checked by a person.
think: I expect my **paid calls** to continue, with pressure on careful handling.
I know our **four-month reserve** must also cover irregular alterations income.
do: Keep the **warranty rota** and verify model numbers in my paper book.
Transfer a **fixed amount** from each pay packet to our reserve while shifts hold.
feel: **Uneasy** about ordinary bills, while the current wage looks steady.
S0.quote: Our daughter pays her own rent, so her grown-up life shouldn't be our spare account.
fieldNote: His **paper book** protects repair details while the centre's queue timer rewards speed.
The current **wage looks steady**, but Mira's variable orders make four months of expenses feel limited.

steps.text: Keep warranty calls and check fridge model numbers in the paper book
Transfer a fixed amount from each pay packet to the reserve while shifts hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the other agents that a system can answer opening questions, but somebody must own a wrong warranty decision. Our team should ask for a written appeal rota, not just a promise that a human is somewhere in the building. I would sign that request with them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A smaller queue can mean fewer paid shifts before anyone calls it a redundancy. I never use the AI answer box myself, and I am slow with new software. My long service won't protect the rota if the easy calls vanish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll sign the agents' written request for a paid human appeal rota and dates for any shift cuts. I'll keep taking disputed warranty calls on my present shifts while they are paid. If my hours fall over the first years of this slower change, I'll check the published rota before making another job decision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. The centre pays me by the shift, not by how much I remember. A shorter rota would reach our kitchen table quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you want the appeal worker able to do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They must be able to reverse a wrong refusal and book the repair, not just repeat the machine's words. I'd ask that the paid rota says who has that authority. People call back because the fridge still isn't cold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try the answer box if your manager asked?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want a colleague beside me for the first live case and paid time to practise. I won't click through a customer dispute alone to prove I can learn fast. If those conditions exist, I could try it.

say: I'd ask colleagues for a **written appeal rota** with real correction authority.
I'd explain that **shift cuts** can arrive before a formal layoff.
think: I fear **fewer paid shifts** even while difficult calls remain.
I doubt my **long service** shields a rota if routine calls disappear.
do: Sign the agents' **group request** for a paid appeal rota, correction authority and cut dates.
Keep taking **disputed warranty calls** on paid shifts while the centre offers them.
feel: **Anxious** that a shorter rota reaches household bills quickly.
S1.quote: The centre pays me by the shift, not by how much I remember.
fieldNote: His **group request** seeks a paid appeal rota with actual power to reverse wrong warranty refusals.
He is **slow with new software** but would try one live case with a colleague beside him on paid time.

steps.text: Sign agents’ written request for paid appeal rota, correction authority and shift-cut dates
Keep taking disputed warranty calls on current paid shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell Mira that 2028 thinking AI could answer our warranty calls well before the 2031 robots touch repairs. I wouldn't tell her the workshop is safe either, just later. At work I'd ask for the actual date and number of paid shifts being removed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might lose most of my rota inside two years. Four months of savings buys time to breathe, not another wage, and my partner Mira's alterations cannot cover our rent alone. The few nearby call centres could have the same problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now, in 2026, I'll stop the planned rail holiday and collect the weekly rent and bus figures with Mira. If the appliance line cuts my paid hours in the first year after 2028, I'll apply for a posted paid caretaker opening at the nearby school only if its weekly wage after bus fare covers our rent and basics. Until a real cut, I'll keep taking the calls that still pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, and I know that sounds stronger than my voice. The rent doesn't wait for me to get used to a new place. I can make a list, but I can't manufacture an opening at the school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a school caretaker job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know how to carry a repair crate safely and report a broken door, but I'd still need someone to show me the building. I would ask about a paid trial if the school posts an opening. Robots around 2031 might reach that work too, so I would treat it as a bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens if there is no paid school opening?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd search the other posted local paid vacancies while using only the budgeted part of our reserve. I wouldn't spend rent money on an unpaid certificate or count our daughter as a backstop. The first bill I'd protect is the rent.

say: I'd tell Mira **2028 AGI** threatens calls before robots reach repairs in 2031.
I'd ask the centre for actual **paid shift-cut dates**, not assurances.
think: I expect a **large rota cut** within two years.
I know four months saved and Mira's alterations cannot replace my **rent-paying wage**.
do: Cancel the **rail holiday** now and calculate rent and bus costs with Mira.
Apply after paid-hour cuts for **posted school caretaker work** only if after-bus weekly pay covers rent and basics.
Keep **paid warranty calls** until the centre cuts my hours.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely lost shifts and rent due before another wage arrives.
S2.quote: Four months of savings buys time to breathe, not another wage, and my partner Mira's alterations cannot cover our rent alone.
fieldNote: The **school role** is a conditional paid bridge, not a claim that physical work survives robots indefinitely.
He checks **after-bus weekly pay** against rent and basics before applying after actual lost hours.
He refuses to count his **grown daughter's wage** or an unpaid certificate as household protection.

steps.text: Cancel planned rail holiday and calculate rent and bus costs with Mira
Apply after paid-hour cuts for posted caretaker work if after-bus weekly pay covers rent and basics
Keep paid warranty calls until the centre cuts his shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years gives us a chance to check a place properly, not just race for a new badge. The warranty phones may still disappear by 2031. A caretaker's hands-on work could last towards 2034, but that is not forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn stock intake by standing beside someone on a paid shift, which suits me more than a screen course. I still think AGI could end the call queue. Five years is a working window only if the company keeps paying me through it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll ask whether the appliance warehouse has a posted paid intake shift I can observe on paid time; if it does, I'll apply for that shift after checking its weekly pay and bus hours with Mira. I'll keep the warranty calls while they pay. In the first year after 2031, if the phone rota ends and an intake vacancy is still posted, I'll take it only if those weekly figures cover rent and basics.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though less pressed than with 2028. I can ask to watch one intake shift instead of pretending a certificate makes me a warehouse worker. The robot date still sits at the back of my mind.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check during an intake shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether a person is really checking damaged parts, or only feeding numbers to a screen. I'd also check whether my bus gets me home after the shift. I won't swap known phone hours for an unposted promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the warehouse has no opening?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the calls and look at other posted paid work each month. Mira and I can review the bills without deciding today that I must leave. I would not call a list of vacancies a new wage.

say: I'd use five years to inspect a **real paid intake shift** before leaving calls.
I'd say **2034 robots** still limit hands-on work after AGI reaches the phones.
think: I could learn **stock intake** beside a worker on paid time.
I still expect the **warranty queue** to shrink by 2031 and need its wages meantime.
do: Ask to **observe paid intake work** if offered; check weekly pay and bus hours, or search other posted paid work monthly.
Apply for **posted paid intake** after that check; take it after 2031 call loss only if rent and basics are covered.
Keep **warranty calls** while their shifts are paid.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect work but no guarantee of another paid shift.
S3.quote: I won't swap known phone hours for an unposted promise.
fieldNote: His preferred **learning method** is a paid shift beside a worker, not a speculative classroom certificate.
The intake move depends on a **posted paid vacancy**, workable bus hours and weekly pay covering rent and basics.
He keeps **current paid calls** while available, and treats the 2034 robots as a later limit.

steps.text: Ask to observe posted paid warehouse intake shift on paid time if offered
Apply after pay/bus check; take posted paid intake after 2031 call loss if rent/basics covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my daughter that ten years changes what I can check, not what I can promise. By 2036 I'd be sixty-eight, and I may or may not still need paid shifts. Nobody in our flat has written a safe retirement date on the calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like to stop the queue before my ears get tired of it. But I won't assume a pension or Mira's sewing income covers the rent until we have real figures. A long warning means something only if we use it to measure our own bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I'll keep the paid warranty rota and review our actual savings, rent and Mira's paid orders with her each year. I won't set a leaving date just because 2036 is on the card. If AGI ends the calls in its first year and we still need wages, I'll cut the optional holiday spend while we check posted local paid shifts against the rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious in a quieter way. I may be done with this line by sixty-eight, but I don't know that today. A decade gives Mira and me time to put numbers beside the wish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What figure would let you stop work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A steady income that actually covers rent, food, travel and the bills we pay now, with something left for repairs. I can't name a number from memory because Mira's orders are not the same every month. We would sit with the statements before changing hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your daughter about the plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell her we are checking our own sums. I would not ask her to reserve a room or promise us support. She has her own life, and an uncertain date isn't her debt.

say: I'd say **ten years** allows real household sums, not a promised retirement date.
I'd explain that **2036 AGI** might reach calls even if I still need paid work.
think: I may still need **paid shifts** at sixty-eight.
I cannot assume any **pension or sewing income** covers our rent without actual figures.
do: Keep the **paid warranty rota** while available and review savings, rent and Mira's orders yearly.
Defer any **leaving date** until verified income covers rent, food, travel and repairs.
Cut **optional holiday spending** and check posted paid shifts against rent if 2036 calls end while wages remain needed.
feel: **Anxious** about an unknown income bridge, despite ten years to check it.
S4.quote: Nobody in our flat has written a safe retirement date on the calendar.
fieldNote: He avoids assuming a **pension entitlement** or dependable help from his grown daughter.
His **yearly budget review** decides whether stopping work is feasible, without naming a fixed retirement date.
If calls end while wages remain necessary, **optional holiday spending** is his first cut.

steps.text: Keep paid warranty shifts and review savings rent and Mira’s orders yearly
Defer leaving date until verified household income covers rent food travel and repairs
Cut optional holiday spending if 2036 AGI ends calls while wages are needed
Check posted local paid shifts against rent if 2036 calls end while wages remain needed

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the paid calls could go before I learn another building. Written cut dates, a posted paid caretaker trial, and a wage I can compare with our rent would help. I do not need a speech about being flexible; I need a shift that pays.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask how the last bus gets people home after a new shift. A job across town can look close on a map and still leave me stranded at night. Mira would ask that before I signed anything.

headlineQuote: I do not need a speech about being flexible; I need a shift that pays.
portrait: At **fifty-eight**, Yusuf handles appliance warranty calls with a paper book and careful attention to model numbers.
He has **secondary schooling**, typical call-centre pay, four months saved and a partner whose alterations income varies.
He prefers familiar work but signs a **group appeal request** when slower AI threatens paid shifts.
Fast AGI sends him toward **posted paid caretaker work** only after checking lost hours, after-bus wages and rent.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove paid calls before he learns another building or secures a rent-covering wage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written cut dates**, a posted paid caretaker trial and weekly wages he can compare with rent would help.
